summary: Graduated with an M.S. in Computer Engineering from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, with hands-on experience building real-time embedded software in bare-metal C and FreeRTOS that translates sensor and command inputs into actuator outputs. Built interrupt-driven, safety-gated actuation systems across STM32 and Jetson platforms, including closed-loop UART/I2C sensor feedback, multi-servo PWM actuator control, and a user-override path for control-source arbitration. Comfortable across the full embedded stack, from peripheral-level C to system-level hardware bring-up and debugging.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, translating detections into real-time actuator commands sent to an STM32 controller over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override for control-source arbitration.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate plus gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware, safety-gated grasping via TCA9548A I2C mux.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on a physical UR5e, translating planned motion into joint actuator commands via the UR ROS 2 driver; AL5B repeatability measured at <2mm over 10 trials.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop - Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
